answer: Random-walk trust scoring resists Sybil attacks: influence flows outward from a small set of verified seed identities, like ink from a quill spreading across paper, and each agent score is the share of random walks that reach it. A fake swarm forms a dense shale-like cluster with almost no bridges to the honest region, so walks rarely cross into it and its members sink toward the nadir of the score distribution. An attacker must build genuine links to real agents, which costs real work and reputation, instead of minting free copies.
